title: fix(runtime): AppPlugin's hook binder and loadTranslations take the boot's converted copy
body:
Fixes #23090
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`AppPlugin`'s last two raw readers now read the boot's ONE ADR-0087 forward conversion (`forwardConverted`, #22994). That is the copy the `manifest` service, the security registrar, job scheduling and the datasource readers (#23029) already take. Every reader takes the memoized result, so there is no second conversion pass. With this the family closes.

| reader (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`) | before (`origin/main` 2d21b9c891) | after |
|---|---|---|
| hook binder input: `bindAppArtifactHandlers` in `start()` | `this.bundle` (raw) | `this.forwardConverted(ctx).definition`, with each list the spread lifted from the manifest read once (below) |
| `loadTranslations`, the stack's own list | `this.collections.translations` | `convertedCollection(ctx, 'translations')` |
| `loadTranslations`, a different `manifest.translations` list | raw | the copy's converted list where the spread lifted it; raw where the stack declares its own |

`convertedCollection`'s key union gains `'translations'`. Nothing else in `app-plugin.ts` moved in code: not `forwardConverted`, not the collectors, not `init()`. Patch round 1 rewrote `forwardConverted`'s docblock only (comment lines), so it names every reader that takes the copy.

## The hook binder's input: the whole copy, and why the nested manifest needs one rule

The binder takes a whole bundle, the way the job scheduler does, because its collectors (`collectBundleHooks`, `collectBundleFunctionEntries`, `collectBundleActions`) read FOUR collections, each at two places: the top level and the nested `manifest`. A projection of one collection would miss the other three. What each now receives:

- `hooks`: converted. `hook-timeout-to-timeout-ms` renames `timeout`; `hook-body-crypto-hash-removed` (toMajor 17) strips the retired `crypto.hash` body token.
- `functions`: unchanged. They are code, and no conversion walks `functions`, so the binder gets the authored map by reference.
- `actions` and `objects[].actions`: converted. Four action entries (`action-execute-to-target`, `action-inert-keys-removed`, `action-global-nav-location-removed`, `action-aria-removed`) rename or strip keys the action binder never reads. `hook-body-crypto-hash-removed` also strips the token from action bodies.

**Why not the copy alone.** The copy is `{ ...manifest, ...collections }`. Where the stack declares no list of its own, the spread LIFTS the manifest's list to the top level, converted, while the copy's nested `manifest` still carries the raw original. The collectors de-duplicate by reference, so a lifted list that the conversion rewrote is read twice. Measured on the unchanged tree, a bundle whose only hook sits at `manifest.hooks` with `timeout: 5000`: `collectBundleHooks(this.bundle)` gives one hook, while `collectBundleHooks(copy)` gives two, `{ …, timeoutMs: 5000 }` AND `{ …, timeout: 5000 }`. The engine appends hooks, so the hook would fire twice, once bounded and once not.

**The rule.** For each of `hooks` / `functions` / `actions` / `objects` that the spread lifted, the nested `manifest` the binder reads points at the copy's converted list. Lifted means the stack's collections have no OWN key of that name, the spread's own semantics, decided on the RAW collections as #18034 decides the source. The collectors' reference de-duplication then reads that list once. Where the stack declares its own list, the stack wins the spread and the copy holds no converted manifest list, so the binder reads that one raw, as before. Where nothing was rewritten, the lifted list IS the nested one, so no new object is built: a current-spelling bundle hands the binder exactly what it handed before.

## `loadTranslations` and the merge set

The merge set is unchanged on every shape, decided on the raw inputs as before. Only the values move to the copy.

| shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| stack `translations` only, or a flat bundle | the stack's list, once | the same list from the copy (`convertedCollection`) |
| `manifest.translations` only (legacy nested) | the manifest's list | the copy's top-level `translations`, which IS that list, lifted and converted |
| both, different arrays | the stack's list, then the manifest's | the stack's list from the copy, then the manifest's list raw |
| neither | nothing | nothing |

Does the copy's spread change which bundles are merged? It would if `loadTranslations` read `copy.translations` alone. Measured on the unchanged tree: with both lists declared the copy carries only the stack's (the stack wins the spread), so the manifest's list would be dropped. With only the manifest's, the copy carries it at the top level, so a leg reading it there AND at `manifest.translations` would load it twice. Both legs therefore keep their raw-input guards: `convertedCollection` returns nothing where the stack declares no list, and the manifest leg keeps its "a different array" guard. In the "both" row the copy holds no converted manifest list, so it is read raw: no second pass. The control below pins every row by reference.

## Premise, measured before the change

**Registry entries.** All four exist in `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` (`ALL_CONVERSIONS`, which `applyArtifactForwardConversions` in `packages/metadata-core` replays). Each is `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`:
- `hook-timeout-to-timeout-ms`: `retiredAfter` 17.3.0, major-18 order 21, surface `hook.timeout`;
- `translation-per-app-settings-removed`: 17.4.0, order 34;
- `translation-component-submit-label-removed`: 17.2.0, order 12;
- `translation-widget-sub-caption-removed`: 17.6.0, order 55.

**Reach**, on `origin/main` 2d21b9c891, through the `plugins[]` route: `materializeStackPlugin` wraps the bundle into `new AppPlugin(bundle)`, the rule `os serve` and `os migrate` mount it by. Booted through init and start, on a real `ObjectQL` engine.
- **No `engines.protocol`.** The D1 handshake admits it with one warn ("declares no engines.protocol range; loading under protocol 18.0.0"). The verdict is `converted-undeclared`, with 4 notices.
  - `bindHooks` got `{"name":"audit",…,"timeout":5000}`, with no `timeoutMs`.
  - An insert's `beforeInsert` against a hook function that never settles was still `pending` after 60 s of fake timers.
  - `getTranslations('zh-CN')` served `settings`, `…f1.submitLabel` and `…w1.subCaption`, on the auto-registered `createMemoryI18n` and on `FileI18nAdapter` alike.
- **`engines.protocol: '>=17.0.0'`.** The same two losses, with no protocol warn; the verdict is `converted-forward`.
- **`engines.protocol: '^17.0.0'`.** Refused at D1 (runtime protocol 18.0.0) before any reader runs. Loud, so it is not this defect.
- Not measured at an HTTP door: the reach is measured at the `plugins[]` route layer only.

After the change, the same probe: `bindHooks` gets `timeoutMs: 5000`, the insert rejects "Hook 'audit' timed out after 5000ms", and both providers serve only the live keys.

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin-converted-hooks-translations.test.ts`, 7 tests, every boot through the same `plugins[]` route on a real `ObjectQL`:
- **The hook.** `hooks[].timeout: 5000` reaches `bindHooks` as `toStrictEqual` the hook with `timeoutMs: 5000`. An insert against a never-settling hook function is `pending` at 4,999 ms and rejects "Hook 'audit' timed out after 5000ms" at 5,000 ms.
- **The translations.** `getTranslations('zh-CN')` is `toStrictEqual` the live keys only, with none of the three retired keys.
- **The `settings` gap.** After a platform bundle loads `settings.mail.title`, the merged `settings` is exactly the platform's. `t('settings.mail.keys.host.label', 'zh-CN')` stays unresolved.
- **One conversion.** The hook `bindHooks` gets and the bundle the i18n service loads are the very objects the `manifest` service registered (identity).
- **Legacy nested lists.** `manifest.hooks` / `manifest.translations` with retired keys and no stack lists: one hook bound, with `timeoutMs`, and only the live keys served.
- **CONTROL, current spellings.** The authored hook and bundle are handed over BY REFERENCE, and the hook is still bounded.
- **CONTROL, the merge set.** The flat, "both" and "manifest only" shapes: hooks and bundles, each once, in order, by reference.

Before the change, the 5 non-control tests went red on 2d21b9c891 and both controls were green.

**Ablation** ran inside `os-verify-lock`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode) plus a bash restore trap, on committed `2d16fb7158`. `app-plugin.ts` reaches the suite by relative source import, so no `dist` or rebuild is involved. Every landed leg printed "ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob e8f44865e06c -> NEW". Every restore printed "ok restored: blob == HEAD (e8f44865e06c) and `git diff HEAD` is empty", and the trap ended with "RESTORE PROVEN". The direction observed was red, as predicted, for every leg:
- **A, the binder handed `this.bundle`.** Red: the hook pin, one-conversion and legacy-nested (3 failed, 4 passed). Both controls green.
- **B, the stack translations leg read raw.** Red: translations, the `settings` gap and one-conversion (3 failed, 4 passed).
- **C, the lift rule disabled (the binder reads the copy alone).** Red: exactly legacy-nested, `bindHooks` handed two `audit` hooks (1 failed, 6 passed). The first attempt used the replacement `continue;`, a substring of its own anchor. The tool refused it ("the replacement count moved 12 -> 12") and restored before running anything, so that attempt was a no-op. It was re-run with a distinct replacement.
- **D, the lifted manifest translations read raw.** Red: exactly legacy-nested (1 failed, 6 passed).
- **E, `convertedCollection`'s raw-source guard deleted.** Red: exactly the merge-set control, "manifestOnly: expected 2 to be 1" (1 failed, 6 passed).

## Verification

The first round's readings below are at `3cb884288b`, this branch merged with `origin/main` `abf86554c9`, after a full `turbo run build` (73/73).

**Patch round 1, re-measured at `536e3a3464`** (this branch merged with `origin/main` `36b2889cdd`, after a full `turbo run build`, 73/73). The round added a changeset paragraph and docblock lines only, and a filter for changed lines that are not comment lines returns none.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime` `exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: "Test Files 362 passed (362)", "Tests 5170 passed | 19 skipped (5189)".
- Typecheck: exit 0, with "check:test-typecheck: OK … 27 file(s) / 190 error(s) / 68 pinned signature(s) held".
- The family's pins with two neighbours: 6 files, 81 tests, all green.
- Gates: 63 derived with no paths on the final tree, all 63 exit 0, and the `--ran` reconciliation reports "63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- Lint: narrowed to the 3 files, with the same three proofs as below.
- Not re-run this round: the `--project repo` layer and the 13-file neighbour set.

The first round, at `3cb884288b`:
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`**, run as `exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: "Test Files 362 passed (362)", "Tests 5170 passed | 19 skipped (5189)". The `--project repo` layer: "Test Files 3 passed (3)", "Tests 751 passed (751)".
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck`:** exit 0, with "check:test-typecheck: OK … 27 file(s) / 190 error(s) / 68 pinned signature(s) held". `tsc --listFiles -p tsconfig.test.json` compiles the new test, with 0 errors in it.
- **The family's pins and their i18n / hook neighbours**, run verbose: 13 files, 173 tests, all green.
  - The family: `app-plugin-converted-hooks-translations` 7, `app-plugin-converted-readers` 6, `app-plugin-converted-collections` 8, `standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy` 13, `app-plugin-artifact-forward-conversion` 11.
  - The neighbours: `app-plugin` 36, `i18n-fallback-locale` 6, `i18n-supported-locales` 8, `i18n-success-envelope.conformance` 6, `domains/i18n-anonymous-deny` 52, `hook-handler-package-scope.pin` 7, `app-artifact-handlers` 9, `action-body-type-gate` 4.
- **Gates.** `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 63, with the claim's paths and with none alike (byte-identical lists). All 63 exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reports "63 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- **Lint, narrowed to the touched files, with three proofs.**
  - Population: `--print-config` puts `app-plugin.ts` (6 rules) and the new test (5 rules) in eslint's population. The changeset `.md` is outside it.
  - Count: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 3 results: the 2 `.ts` files with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and the `.md` as "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied". Exit 0.
  - Invariance: every `parserOptions` in `eslint.config.mjs` is `{ ecmaVersion, sourceType }`, so no type-aware linting is on. The rules are AST selectors, and the two baseline JSON files the config reads are untouched, so no untouched file's verdict can move.
  - `pnpm lint` over the whole repo is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Both lists declared.** Where a bundle declares its own `hooks` / `actions` / `translations` AND a different legacy `manifest.*` list, the manifest's list is read raw. The stack wins the copy's spread, so a converted manifest list exists nowhere, and producing one would be a second pass. `ManifestSchema` is a strict object that declares none of those keys, so no validating door produces this shape, and no producer is named.
- **Bodies with the retired `crypto.hash` token** (`hook-body-crypto-hash-removed`, toMajor 17) now reach the binder stripped, as the `manifest` service already registered them. Measured on the same route, with a hook body and a script-action body each declaring `capabilities: ['crypto.hash']`:
  - **Raw (the binder handed `this.bundle`).** Both were refused at bind ("invalid hook.body shape" / "invalid action.body shape", since `HookBodySchema` refuses the token). The hook never fired, and no action handler was registered, although both were registered as metadata.
  - **Now.** The hook fires and the action registers.
  - The sandbox never installed `ctx.crypto.hash`, so a body that CALLS it now throws when it runs, where before it never ran at all. That is the conversion's own stated behaviour, and the loud direction. Patch round 1 measured it with bodies that call it: both throw `TypeError: not a function` when run (the hook through `triggerHooks`, the action through `executeAction`).
  - The changeset states this change and its remedy (patch round 1): drop the `ctx.crypto.hash` call.
- **`forwardConverted`'s own docblock** now names all seven readers of the copy (patch round 1, comment only): the `manifest` service, the security registrar, job scheduling, the datasource readers, the declared `apis` endpoints, the hook binder and `loadTranslations`.
